The ingots with a nominal composition of CoCrFeNiTi0.2 (in atomic percent, at.%) were prepared by vacuum arc melting under a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere. After being repeatedly melted five times
the ingots were then drop-casted into a water-cooled copper mold with a dimension of 85 × 10 × 2 mm3.
The as-cast plates were homogenized at 1473 K for 5 h ... All heat treatments were conducted in air and followed by water quenching.
and then cold-rolled with a total reduction ratio of 60% (the thickness changed from 2 to 0.8 mm).

evidence.quote: There are two kinds of precipitates in the alloy, i.e., lamellar (Regions I) and spherical (Regions II). The width of lamellar precipitates is about 30–100 nm, while the length is between several hundred nanometers and several micrometers.

Fig. 1 (b) shows the OM images of the homogenized and aged samples, which are all uniform equiaxed crystal microstructures. The grains of the homogenized samples are relatively coarse, and the average grain size is about 135 μm.
In addition, a large number of annealing twins exist in these samples, suggesting that the stacking fault energy of the current HEA are relatively low.

mechanisms.name: stacking fault formation

evidence.quote: At 77 K, the density of stacking faults in the current HEA increases greatly, as shown in Fig. 5(c), which is due to the corresponding decrease of stacking fault energy when the temperature decreases.

mechanisms.name: twin formation suppression
mechanisms.material_state: aged at 1173 K for 10 min, tested at 77 K

evidence.quote: The inhibition of deformation twins is mainly due to two reasons. On the one hand, L12-type precipitates have high stacking fault energy. ... On the other hand, fine nano-precipitates will hinder the formation of twins.
